title: Native public HTTPS release identity and content-integrity qualification
summary: RasenFalcon v0.4.5 implements a live public HTTPS probe that uses platform TLS validation or explicit CA and optional leaf fingerprint, then compares nine page bodies and four static assets against a pinned local build. Tests use a localhost TLS server, not the production native ooRexx server. Autobuilder is offline and no live host was contacted.
invariants: A 200 response is not proof of the intended published site: verify the exact 13 path bytes against SHA-256.
Verify the TLS certificate chain, intended hostname/SNI and TLS minimum 1.2; no -k, plaintext HTTP or redirect fallback.
The operator CLI accepts only rasenfalcon.com and www.rasenfalcon.com for public endpoint checks, and refuses arbitrary IP targets.
Do not issue an unknown-route probe on a live protected service: the owned HTTPS hostile-source firewall may block that test source.
Local source integrity and remote response integrity are separately verified; a source-manifest mismatch or remote body alteration is FAIL.

The test fixture uses an ephemeral localhost TLS server and tests invalid trust, hostname, leaf fingerprint, redirects and tampered content; these tests prove the probe, not a running ooRexx HTTPS service.
Even if content_integrity=PASS, CMS/Brand/Wire release authorized, private mTLS, installed systemd and production approval remain NOT_TESTED.
Public apex is not equivalent to NOC or Office; those must separately require client mTLS with owner-private CA, LDAP active principal and HTTPS_LOGIN.
Source v0.4.5 test run: website 18/18 and handoff/deployment 38/38 locally PASS, including 9 local TLS-fixture tests; live public HTTPS NOT_RUN.

provenance.claim: Executable 13-path HTTPS identity, TLS and body verification.
Ephemeral TLS success and negative qualification.
